 Soccer-Ronaldinho poised for Ravenna start and, perhaps, one last goal
 Saturday, 14 Nov 2026
 | 2:20 AM MYT
 share 
 bookmark 
 FILE PHOTO: Soccer Football - Ronaldinho to appear at Ravenna FC team presentation - Stadio Bruno Benelli, Ravenna, Italy - August 20, 2026 Ronaldinho poses as he is presented as a new player for Ravenna FC REUTERS/Ciro De Luca/File Photo 
 Nov 13 (Reuters) - Ronaldinho will roll ⁠back the years this weekend when the 46-year-old Brazilian starts his ⁠first competitive match in over a decade, and in the unlikely ‌setting of an Italian third-tier derby the World Cup winner may realise his dream of scoring one last time.
 The Brazil great and Ballon d'Or winner signed for Ravenna in June, ​also taking a stake in the club, but ⁠because he had not played since ⁠his final appearance for Fluminense in 2015, doubts remained over whether fans would ⁠ever ‌see him in action.
 Ravenna revealed three weeks ago that the former Barcelona and AC Milan player would make his return in Sunday's ⁠home clash with local rivals Forli, and on Friday, ​manager Andrea Mandorlini ‌told reporters that Ronaldinho would start the match.
 "He will play from the ⁠start, there's ​no doubt," Mandorlini said.
 "Then together we will decide how long he plays. He is one of the greatest players of the modern era. And we have to get ⁠a result. We always play with three forwards. ​He will be one of the three."
 Ronaldinho was welcomed by the Ravenna fans in August, without committing to a return to the pitch. He returned to ⁠Italy on Friday afternoon and will have just one training session with his teammates on Saturday before making his club debut.
 A temporary stand has been erected at the Stadio Bruno Benelli to cater for the crowd, and if ​this does turn out to be one last hurrah ⁠for Ronaldinho, he may well get the chance to score his 300th professional ​goal.
 Simone Rabbi will play alongside the Brazilian up ‌front for Ravenna, and in Friday's press ​conference he said that if his side are awarded a penalty on Sunday, Ronaldinho will take the spot kick.
 (Reporting by Trevor Stynes)
